items.title: NVIDIA DGX Spark Developer Kit Turns a Desk Into a Supercomputing Lab
items.summary_1line: At SC26, an annual supercomputing conference taking place this week in Chicago, NVIDIA is introducing the DGX Spark HPC Developer Kit for researchers, academics and developers. The kit is a four-node cluster of NVIDIA...
items.editor_note: Moves the thread from one box to a four-node cluster kit announced at SC26.

editorial.tldr: By Oct 28, vLLM's CI was testing DGX Spark, and NVIDIA was shipping the related RTX Spark laptops from six OEMs. On Nov 2, NVIDIA added Flare, a DGX Spark inference engine, and a guide to running a 124B MoE model on one box.
editorial.whats_new: At SC26 on Nov 16, NVIDIA introduced the DGX Spark HPC Developer Kit, a four-node DGX Spark cluster aimed at researchers and developers.
editorial.why_it_matters: DGX Spark is moving from a single desk box to a small multi-node target, so local serving work now covers both single-box MoE tuning and cross-node setups.
editorial.take_for_builders: If you target DGX Spark, benchmark Flare against your pinned vLLM build on one box first; hold multi-node plans until the kit's interconnect and serving support are documented.

status.detail: NVIDIA keeps adding DGX Spark tooling and hardware configurations; no independent benchmarks are in the thread yet.
